The LR/SC sequence can be given acquire semantics by setting the aq bit on the LRinstruction. The LR/SC sequence can be given release semantics by by setting the rl_

_bit on the SC instruction.
grades.reason: Identifies aq as acquire and rl as release for LR/SC, but does not explain their individual AMO ordering guarantees.
Maps aq to acquire, rl to release, and aqrl to both, without explaining the ordering effects.

grades.quote: TSO atomic read-modify-writes and x86 instructions using the LOCK prefix are fully ordered and can be implemented either via an AMO with both _aq_ and _rl_ set, or via an LR with _aq_ set, the arithmetic operation in question, an SC with both _aq_ and _rl_ set, and a conditional branch checking the success condition.
grades.reason: Explains that both bits provide fully ordered AMOs, but not what each bit does individually.

grades.quote: If the _aq_ bit is set, then no later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place before the AMO. Conversely, if the _rl_ bit is set, then other RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding the AMO in this RISC-V hart. Setting both the _aq_ and the _rl_ bit on an AMO makes the sequence sequentially consistent, meaning that it cannot be reordered with earlier or later memory operations from the same hart.
grades.reason: Directly explains the ordering effects of aq, rl, and their combination on RISC-V AMOs.
